stem:
Lalit looks at the figure: line AOB is straight through O, and ray OC meets AOB so that angle $1$ equals angle $2$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Angle $1$ is a right angle for any split of AOB, even when angle $1$ is not half of the straight angle.
He should first study the decorative history of the diagram before classifying any angle.
AOB is a straight angle (a half turn); because angle $1$ equals angle $2$, each is a right angle, so OC is perpendicular to AOB.
The answer is "straight angle", because those words are printed beside AOB, without using the equal split.

teacher.key_rationale: A straight angle is a half turn; an equal split makes two right angles; lines meeting at right angles are perpendicular. Skipping the half-turn condition, citing history, or grabbing the printed label miss the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Straight line AOB with ray OC upright; angles 1 and 2 marked equal.
